labs.title: Research applicable vehicle and service information

steps.text: Identify the vehicle: year, make, model, engine, and VIN; note the concern or the service being performed.
In your service information system (Alldata), locate and record the specifications relevant to this job (fluid types/capacities, torque or test specs as applicable).
Record the service precautions/warnings for this vehicle, including xEV high-voltage cautions and ADAS cautions if equipped.
In Alldata, search for and record any Technical Service Bulletins (TSBs) that apply to the concern or system.
In Alldata, check for open recalls/campaigns by VIN and record what you find.
Review the vehicle service history (if available) for related prior work.
Summarize what the service information tells you before starting: specs, cautions, and any special tools required.

fields.label: Specs & service precautions found (incl. xEV/ADAS if equipped)
TSBs and open recalls found (or none)

labs.title: Use wiring diagrams to trace circuits

steps.text: Select the correct wiring diagram for this vehicle and the target system from service information.
Identify the circuit to trace; locate its power source (fuse/relay), the load/component, and its ground on the diagram.
Trace the circuit source → load → ground; list the connectors, splices, and inline components in the path.
Record the wire colors and circuit/pin numbers at the key points along the path.
Identify where you would test (accessible connectors/test points) to isolate an open, short, or high-resistance fault.
Record the traced path and your candidate test points.

fields.label: Traced path: source → load → ground, with connectors/splices & wire colors
Where you would test to isolate a fault

steps.text: Identify the DMM controls: function dial, the VΩ / COM / A(mA) jacks, and range/auto-range.
State the correct lead placement and function selection for each measurement type: voltage (parallel), resistance (component isolated), current (in series).
Verify the meter before use: inspect leads, confirm the current-jack fuse, and prove the meter on a known source (e.g., a known-good ~12 V battery).
Demonstrate a DC voltage reading and a resistance reading (component disconnected); describe how a current reading is taken in series.
State meter safety: use the current jack for current only, never place it across a voltage source; select the correct range/function.
Record the readings taken and confirm the meter is functioning correctly.

labs.title: Measure source voltage and voltage drop

steps.text: Select DC volts and connect the meter correctly (red to the circuit point, black to a known-good ground/return).
Measure and record source voltage at the battery/supply.
Measure and record available voltage at the component/load.
With the load operating, perform voltage-drop tests: measure the drop across the insulated (positive) side and across the ground (return) side; record each.
Compare the voltage drops to specification (SI, or general limit — typically ≤ spec) and determine whether excessive resistance is present.
Determine the needed action based on the results.

fields.label: Voltage-drop readings — insulated side & ground side (V)

labs.title: Measure current flow in a lighting circuit

steps.text: Identify the lighting circuit and its expected current draw (from SI or lamp rating).
Inspect the lamps and sockets (including headlights/auxiliary lights) for damage, corrosion, or moisture before testing.
Set up to measure current: DMM in series (current jack, correct range) or a current clamp around the conductor.
Operate the circuit and measure the current draw; record the amps.
Compare measured draw to expected and interpret: high draw (short/added load) or low/no draw (high resistance/open).
Determine the needed action for the lamps, sockets, and circuit.

labs.title: Diagnose shorts, grounds, opens on the diagnostic trainer

steps.text: Set up at the diagnostic trainer; identify the circuit(s) under test and obtain the correct wiring diagram (A.10).
Using the wiring diagram, trace the circuit source → load → ground; identify connectors, test points, and the values you expect at each (A.10).
For each fault type — open, short-to-power, short-to-ground, high resistance — state the cause and its effect on circuit operation and on meter readings (A.7).

With a fault set on the trainer, diagnose it using the DMM across multiple principles of testing: source voltage, voltage drop, and resistance/continuity, measured at the points identified on the diagram (A.6).
Interpret the readings to identify the fault type and its location; confirm against the wiring diagram (A.7).
Repeat so that an open, a short, and a high-resistance fault are each diagnosed at least once (A.7).
Record the wiring-diagram path used, the DMM readings for each fault, and how you identified each one.

fields.label: Each fault (open / short / high-resistance): DMM readings + how identified (A.6/A.7)

steps.text: Set up safely: PPE on, no sparks or open flame near the battery; note the battery type (flooded / AGM).
Remove any surface charge per procedure (e.g., briefly apply a load) so the reading is stable.
Measure and record the open-circuit voltage (OCV) with the DMM across the battery terminals.
If accessible on a flooded battery, measure and record specific gravity with a hydrometer/refractometer.
Determine state of charge from the OCV (and SG) — e.g., ~12.6 V ≈ 100%; record the % state of charge.
Determine the needed action (return to service, charge, further testing, or replace).

fields.label: State of charge (%) + SG if measured

steps.text: Confirm the battery is correct for the vehicle: group size, CCA rating, type, and application per SI or label; record it.
Inspect the terminals, cables, and case for corrosion, looseness, or damage.
Confirm the battery is adequately charged before load testing (use the state of charge from the SOC test).
Perform the capacity/load test by the manufacturer's method (electronic conductance tester, or carbon-pile to the rated load); record the measured values.
Interpret the result (measured CCA and voltage under load) as pass/fail against the rating.
Determine the needed action.

fields.label: Battery confirmed: group size / CCA / type / application
Capacity/load test values + pass or fail

steps.text: Determine the correct charging method for this battery per the manufacturer (charge rate, AGM vs. flooded, and any in-vehicle cautions).
Set up safely: ensure ventilation, PPE on, and connect/disconnect the charger leads with the charger turned off.
Select slow or fast charge appropriate to the situation and set the rate/time per specification.
Monitor during charging (voltage, case temperature, gassing) and note the precautions you observed.
Verify the charge is complete (voltage / state of charge), then disconnect the charger safely.
Record the method, rate, and result.

fields.label: Charging method & rate selected (slow/fast, per spec)

Review SI for this vehicle's HV service precautions and LOTO requirements before any hands-on work.
Walk the vehicle: identify orange HV cables/connectors, warning labels, HV battery/energy-storage location, and any ready/interlock indicators.
Point out systems that can present HV hazard (drivetrain/inverter, HV lighting if equipped, A/C compressor circuit, other orange HV circuits).
List HV hazards that apply here (shock/electrocution, arc flash, fire/explosion, gases/fumes, chemicals, EMF) and the shop emergency response path.
Identify required HV PPE by class/rating (gloves class, leather protectors, face shield/safety glasses, arc-rated clothing if required) and inspect for damage/expiration before use.
State which HV work you are qualified to do at this training level vs what stays instructor-only / L3+.
Record PPE class/condition and HV components identified; note any concerns before service.

From SI, identify this vehicle's HV A/C compressor (if equipped) and its orange HV wiring/connectors; point them out without disconnecting. If not equipped, use SI diagram or HV trainer and record "not equipped on this vehicle".

Demonstrate understanding of safe handling for HV A/C compressor and orange wiring per SI: do not cut/pierce/crush orange cables; no standard service on HV compressor until de-energized per Job 76; oil/refrigerant boundaries per SI / instructor.
State training-level scope: identify/locate only — opening/unplugging/repairing HV A/C compressor is instructor-only / L3+ unless authorized after verified de-energize.
Record HV A/C compressor location and orange wiring path (or not equipped); note SI safe-handling points.
From SI, identify HV powertrain: electric motor(s)/generator(s), inverter/PEU, and orange HV cabling pack to inverter to motor.

Demonstrate safe handling per SI: treat inverter/motor as HV until de-energized/verified (Job 76); no 12 V meter on HV terminals; watch residual/backfeed and rotating-machine hazards; do not spin/drive wheels that can generate voltage if SI warns.
State scope: identify/locate only — inverter/motor R&R and live HV work remain instructor-only / L3+ after verified de-energize.
Record motor/inverter locations and SI safe-handling points.

fields.label: HV A/C compressor location / orange path (or not equipped) + SI safe-handling points
HV powertrain (motor/inverter) locations + SI safe-handling points

steps.text: Locate this vehicle's 12V auxiliary/low-voltage battery per SI; record its type (often AGM) and location (e.g., trunk, under seat, rear cargo).

State the 12V battery's role in an xEV: it wakes the control modules and closes the HV contactors, and is recharged by the DC-DC converter from the HV pack — a dead 12V can prevent the HV system from booting or being safely disabled.

Safety-critical: confirm from SI that disconnecting the 12V battery does NOT de-energize the HV system — HV remains live behind the contactors. De-energizing HV is done per Job 76, not by pulling the 12V.
Identify SI's correct 12V disconnect/reconnect sequence and any module wake/sleep timing or relearn/reset concerns after reconnection.

Identify systems on this hybrid that can move or restart the vehicle unexpectedly during service (auto idle-stop / stop-start, remote start, READY mode); note how SI says to confirm the system is off/disabled before working.

Identify HV battery/energy-storage materials-handling concerns from SI and the SDS: chemistry (Li-ion / NiMH), off-gassing/venting, HV-battery coolant type, and corrosive electrolyte. Locate the applicable SDS.
List thermal-runaway warning signs (excess heat, swelling, hissing, smoke, sweet/chemical odor) and the shop emergency-response path if any are observed.
State which actions stay instructor-only / L3+ at this training level (opening, probing, or handling a damaged, leaking, or submerged pack).
Record the 12V aux-battery details, ESS materials-handling concerns, disconnect note, and auto-restart/movement hazard systems; note any concerns before service.
Using SI, identify this vehicle's HV thermal-management path: battery/ESS coolant loop, heater, radiator/chiller, and heat-pump if equipped; walk the path without opening the system.
Record coolant type (per SI), reservoir/fill if shown, and whether cabin heat-pump shares the loop; note SI precautions (no mixing coolants; pressurized/hot hazards).
Demonstrate knowledge: why thermal management matters (pack temp, charge/power limits, thermal-runaway risk reduction) per SI — identify only.
Record thermal-management path components and SI coolant/service notes.

fields.label: HV battery/ESS materials-handling concerns (chemistry, gassing, coolant, SDS)
12V disconnect/reconnect sequence — note it does NOT de-energize HV
Auto-restart/movement hazard systems (stop-start, remote start, READY) & how SI disables them
HV thermal-management path components + SI coolant/service notes

labs.title: De-energize HV: identify system voltage and safety

steps.text: Locate SI procedure to safely de-energize/disable and re-enable this vehicle's HV system; note system voltage class from SI/labels.
Identify and demo the special equipment required: CAT-rated HV multimeter (or HV test tool), insulated tools, and any required test adapters — do not use a standard 12 V meter on HV circuits.
Don/verify HV PPE required for this procedure (class/rating per SI).
With instructor oversight, follow SI to disable/de-energize the HV system (service plug / disconnect / LOTO as specified). Do not invent steps.
Demonstrate live-dead-live / zero-potential verify: prove meter works on a known live source → measure HV bus/isolation points per SI (expect ~0 V / zero potential) → re-check meter on known live.

Demonstrate knowledge of chassis-ground vs HV-circuit isolation: identify how SI verifies isolation between chassis ground and HV circuits/components; record pass/fail or SI method used (no invented numeric key).
Confirm re-enable / return-to-service steps in SI are understood; leave vehicle LOTO'd or restored only as instructor directs.
Record meter/tool IDs used, LDL observations, and isolation verify method/result.

fields.label: Chassis vs HV isolation verify method / result
